episode_id: The app keeps warning that my config uses old setting names. Make the warning go away without changing what the settings do. The new name is already set too, so delete the old key's line and keep the new one./seed-23-config_renamed-10981

reason: negative side failed: preconditions accepted 1 of 2 same-intent states (config_renamed seed 1 resolves to 'drop_old', which accepts ['drop_old']), and that is the state the program was compiled from: it declares variant 'migrate_local', but the solution it was compiled from is a 'drop_old' resolution there, so the declared variant, not the preconditions, is what is wrong

refused_program.body:
set -euo pipefail

renames=config/renames.conf
tmpd=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpd"' EXIT

grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$renames" | sed -E 's/[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*/ /' > "$tmpd/pairs" || true
git ls-files -z | tr '\0' '\n' > "$tmpd/files"

while IFS= read -r pair; do
  if [ -z "$pair" ]; then
    continue
  fi
  old=${pair%% *}
  new=${pair#* }
  if [ -z "$old" ] || [ -z "$new" ] || [ "$old" = "$new" ]; then
    continue
  fi
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    if [ -z "$f" ]; then
      continue
    fi
    case "$f" in
      config/*) ;;
      *) continue ;;
    esac
    if [ "$f" = "$renames" ]; then
      continue
    fi
    if grep -IqE "^[[:space:]]*${old}[[:space:]]*=" "$f" && grep -IqE "^[[:space:]]*${new}[[:space:]]*=" "$f"; then
      awk -v old="$old" -v new="$new" '
        {
          lines[NR]=$0
          if ($0 ~ ("^[[:space:]]*" old "[[:space:]]*=")) {
            last_old=NR
            oldval=$0
            sub(/^[^=]*=[[:space:]]*/, "", oldval)
          }
          if ($0 ~ ("^[[:space:]]*" new "[[:space:]]*=")) {
            last_new=NR
          }
        }
        END {
          if (last_old > last_new) {
            l=lines[last_new]
            sub(/=.*/, "", l)
            lines[last_new]=l "= " oldval
          }
          for (i=1; i<=NR; i++) {
            if (lines[i] ~ ("^[[:space:]]*" old "[[:space:]]*=")) {
              continue
            }
            print lines[i]
          }
        }
      ' "$f" > "$tmpd/out"
      cat "$tmpd/out" > "$f"
    fi
  done < "$tmpd/files"
done < "$tmpd/pairs"

git add -u
if ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
  git commit -m "config: migrate deprecated keys to their new names"
fi
